purpose: Where Rubin and the reference disagree, rendered so it can be viewed over the star image rather than inferred by comparing two frames by eye.

scaling.unit: empirically measured scatter of the smoothed difference, per region
scaling.why: The propagated variance planes understate the true uncertainty on these products by a median factor of about seven, so a map scaled by them would paint ordinary noise as a discovery.

peakClassification.onSource: The peak sits on Rubin flux above the 98th percentile of the field. PSF matching is never exact in a bright core, so these are real disagreements that say more about the match than about the sky.
peakClassification.offSource: The peak sits away from bright flux. These are the ones worth looking at, and they are still not detections: the bandpass caveat below applies to every pixel.

crossBandNote: A few regions compare Rubin against a reference in a different filter -- r against z in one case. Those frames disagree everywhere for a trivial reason, and the explorer labels them so a large difference is not mistaken for an interesting one.
caveat: Bandpass transfer is not validated for these pairs: a single linear colour term does not describe it, with a reduced chi-square of 93.8 over 112 fields. A genuine colour difference between two surveys produces exactly this signal. These maps show where two images disagree, not where the sky is unusual.
